did_you_know.text: The issue was brought by family heads — showing how Israel’s tribal system handled public matters through appointed family representatives.
The case of Zelophehad’s daughters set an important legal precedent: when there were no sons, daughters could inherit — one of the clearer biblical examples of inheritance rights for women.
The rule forbidding transfer of land between tribes aimed to preserve tribal borders and the link between land and tribal identity — land was central to Israel’s social and economic structure.
The daughters’ names are recorded (Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah); some of these names appear elsewhere in the Bible — for example, 'Tirzah' is also used as a place-name.
